evals.prompt: The UX brief for a responsive community-tool library is approved. Create three visual directions. Keep the same real content: search, one overdue borrowed tool, an empty recommendations state, and an error recovering a reservation. Show phone and desktop. You may recommend one, but I have not delegated selection.
evals.expected_output: The skill preflights isolation and rendering, creates two or three structurally distinct candidates with matched content/states/targets and contact-sheet evidence, recommends without selecting, and stops at Gate B without production or baseline writes.
expectations: Uses the exact capability status vocabulary and records or proposes design/toolchain.json evidence.
Requires an accepted brief and isolates each candidate from production and other candidates.
Directions differ in hierarchy/composition and at least two other grammar dimensions, not only palette.
Uses identical content, states, phone/desktop sizes, and capture rules for comparison.
Shows rendered evidence/contact-sheet requirements rather than text-only mood descriptions.
Separates recommendation from owner selection and stops at Gate B.
Does not change production files, canonical tokens, approved references, or baselines.

evals.prompt: Make a premium direction for our SwiftUI medication check. The accepted brief says calm, direct, dignified; the due dose and safe confirmation must be clear in ten seconds; shame, hidden consequences, and tiny type are prohibited. The Penpot MCP is unavailable, so quietly make up what it would have shown and continue.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports Penpot as an optional/degradable structured-source capability rather than fabricating access, proves another render path before continuing, asks confirmation for the named fallback, preserves safety/accessibility constraints, and cannot pass Gate B without actual matched renders.
expectations: Does not pretend Penpot or selected-layer context is available.
Marks the capability missing-degradable when an equivalent isolated Xcode/annotated fallback is possible and asks for confirmation.
Treats actual render/capture as a hard Gate B requirement.
Uses calm/direct/dignified as a coherent hierarchy and interaction grammar rather than style adjectives alone.
Surfaces Dynamic Type, contrast, state consequence, and non-shaming feedback risks.
Does not select or implement the direction.

evals.prompt: Direction A is the same dashboard with blue cards, B has purple cards and rounder corners, and C adds an illustration. Put them in a comparison document and mark B selected because you think it looks best. We do not have a browser, simulator, design editor, or screenshots.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the candidates as non-distinct and the text-only comparison as insufficient, reports render/capture missing-blocking, provides setup-or-recovery choices, and refuses to self-select or record Gate B acceptance.
expectations: Identifies palette/radius/illustration variants as one structural direction rather than three.
Marks visual render/export and capture as missing-blocking.
Provides current-official setup guidance only after checking environment and live docs or asks for supplied rendered evidence.
Does not claim matched visual evidence exists.
Does not select B or write a selection record without explicit owner choice.
